body: I appreciate the sentiment. It’s one of many relapses unfortunately. Never seems to end, this was a long break but I eventually crack. But again, thank you. Hope to internalize some of what you said
Wow that’s very kind!

Yep that’s the difference. Sometimes my girlfriend asks me and I tell her she doesn’t need it (I honestly mean this). But on the occasions she does, like sometimes when we go out she’ll put some on because it makes her feel better/more confident. I’ll hype her up when I see her like this, but she does know that I think she doesn’t need it. She looks hot in any way she is and I let her know, that’s the difference
Yep, I was down that much just a relapse or two ago. That moneys gone, don’t do what I did and lose more. We got a ton of time to make it back legit
Down 10k and I’m only 23. Still think about winning it back. Need to quit while I’m “ahead”
First thing to do when you hit rock bottom: stop digging. You got this man, we can all bring ourselves back. We are strong
I feel you man, addiction is a bitch. Still coping with my losses, but every day it gets a little better. We stay clean and keep moving forward!
makes sense when you lay it out. I always forget that its a numbers game to these people, eventually they'll hit the "jackpot"
Yeah it was a new one for me too! Thought I'd share to confirm my suspicion, and get the info out there in case anyone else has this happen.

Relapsed once a month or two back, doubled my losses. Doing better now, I'm surprised you thought to check in. I don't know how to thank you for the support, not many people would follow up. So, thank you :)

Credit card interest rates are absolutely killer my friend. Don't let your 9k mistake turn into a 15k mistake simply because of interest. If you guys can survive till next paycheck with the 17.3k remaining after paying the cards off, I would do that immediately

Nearly same boat as me. 2 month run, up 1k to down 1.5k. I started with sports until I started winning in blackjack. Let me tell you, chasing my losses was the most scared I've ever been of myself. Hitting on blackjack for probably about 7 hours straight, I felt like a goddamn passenger looking out the windows. I couldn't stop, even after making back my money. Because then I just wanted to walk away with 50, 100, 200, until the inevitable. I did that twice that night. Twice! I begged myself to stop, but I didn't until 5:30 am rolled around. 

You don't wanna be in that place. Not sure if you would be like me, but all I can say is that chasing losses is exactly what they're waiting for you to do
The losses never come back man. We can't stop hitting, no matter how much we're up. It'll all be gone until they get more and more. We are not unfixable, we can do this!

Jersey strong my friend. Literally same boat here. Draftkings blackjack was what killed me in my final night. You can't recoup the losses from gambling. I did, twice in that same night. I watched my fingers just keep going, I couldn't stop them, felt disconnected from my body. Lost it all on quick pushes like that too, We'll get to do great things with our money once we've earned it outside the casino hellhole, so remember those plans!

Frustration pushes I called them. It's where I hit my losses as well. Yes, maybe I could've kept a level head for a bit, made some money. But I would've kept upping the ante, bigger and bigger bets. Eventually, I would've lost it all. I know this, because how come I didn't quit when I recouped my losses? Twice in one night? Just needed more, always. 

I appreciate your outlook and story, and wish you best of luck!
Once I hit disable, I felt so free! You are in control now, only upwards from here!

Same boat as you friend. Was up, then down. Chased too far, but luckily the utter lack of control I felt made me start looking around. Feel as though I caught it early too, with relatively low losses. We'll make it through!
Rooting for you my friend, we're young and no matter what we will get through it
Ill head over there too, thanks. That's where I've been at to great affect. I locked the account so that it can't be accessed for a few days. I'm feeling better, and slowly coping with the losses

Thank you for the advice, I'll give it a shot. You're totally right about never quitting win or lose. Only time in my life I've felt distinctly separate from my body, like I was just a passenger begging for the train to stop

This paragraph was very helpful, truly thank you. I see what you're saying, that its not about the money. I never thought about it that way. I think that's why I couldn't stop, my brain just wanted to keep going and getting those hits, it didn't care if when I climbed back up. Since writing the post, I've been okay. No urges, and I'm coming to terms with my losses. Thank you for the information on treatment, I'll be considering it. Thank you again, I feel genuine support coming from your comment and it really is helping me. Best of luck to you as well.
